decision.rationale: The remediation fixes authoritative event semantics and Claude transcript correlation, and both real client records pass. PRR-001 remains blocking because the CODEX path derives replay objectives from any parsed POST while accepting the claimed operation solely from public authority; the two facts need not be the same request.

summary: Cycle 4 further narrows PRR-001 but does not close the client-execution correlation required by AC-15. Approval remains withheld only because a Codex transcript can execute/replay one operation while a different authoritative operation is accepted as the claimed client request.

findings.title: Codex replay evidence is not bound to the accepted request claim
findings.observation: Every COMMITTED claim is checked against the authoritative operation, but exact transcript matching is conditional on client === CLAUDE. For CODEX, unknown-result-replayed and exact-body-key-reused are granted when any same-signature curl POST pair has timeout/success markers; the replay path is never compared with the record's accepted claim.
findings.trigger: Provide a real authoritative Idea creation request ID and resource, while the Codex transcript contains the IDs but its only timeout/replay POST pair targets a different non-human operation such as a Project transition.
findings.impact: The verifier returns PASS even though Codex did not execute the request claimed by the committed evidence record. Live authority plus an unrelated client replay can therefore be assembled into a compatibility pass, which violates AC-15's requirement for an actual representative client execution and the approved no-static-substitution gate.

evidence.description: At the exact head, a structurally valid CODEX transcript replayed only POST /api/v1/projects/{otherProject}/transitions. The public fixture contained a real IDEA_CREATED request, and the record claimed POST /api/v1/ideas status 201. verifyClientEvidence returned accepted=true with all CODEX objectives.
evidence.reference: reviewer Codex cross-operation counterexample at fdeb033a20c6efcbe0ff65202a20258032b862e1

evidence.description: The authoritative operation check is followed by a transcript-claim check only for CLAUDE; CODEX immediately continues after the authority match.
CODEX replay objectives are added from codexFacts booleans without comparing codexFacts.postPaths to requestClaims.
The Cycle 4 negatives vary the claim against authority but keep the same Codex create-Idea replay transcript; no test varies the transcript operation independently from the authoritative claim.

Both exact committed records independently pass against their real ignored transcripts and the live proof API, so the positive evidence path works; the failure is specifically the missing Codex cross-correlation discriminator.
AC-15 requires each named client to actually execute the representative validation, and the plan disallows a hand-written assertion without live request/resource correlation.

findings.remediation: Parse a Codex POST/response fact for the accepted request, or otherwise bind the Codex replay tuple to the corresponding requestClaim. Require the transcript-observed method, exact path, terminal status and request ID to agree with the same authoritative operation; keep the existing body/key replay and live-resource checks. Add a cross-operation negative where authority and transcript are each individually valid but describe different requests.
findings.verification: Both current real client records still pass; the exact previous same-resource negatives fail; and a Codex transcript that replays a Project transition cannot authorize an Idea-creation claim even when the Idea request ID and resource are real.

findings.title: Child-resource writes are committed without matching public reads
findings.observation: The current implementation maps every scenario result ref to a direct or paginated public read and requires an exact ID match.
findings.trigger: A normal, recovered or terminal-replayed journal entry contains a child resource reference.
findings.impact: The exact child must be publicly present before COMMITTED/PASS; missing or mismatched children now fail closed.

evidence.description: Exact report/progress reads pass, mismatched progress fails, and terminal replay performs zero writes while reading reports and progress.

findings.verification: Targeted unit tests and exact-head CI verify normal, recovery and terminal readback behavior.

findings.title: IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS is persisted as terminal rejection
findings.observation: The current recovery helper recognizes the bounded retry contract, preserves exact bytes/key and leaves exhaustion OUTCOME_UNKNOWN.
findings.trigger: Recovery receives one or more 409 IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS responses.
findings.impact: Temporary concurrency no longer becomes terminal local rejection and the original intent remains resumable.

evidence.description: The exact-head regression proves retry-success after two sends and OUTCOME_UNKNOWN after three bounded in-progress responses, with identical body and key.

findings.verification: Targeted unit tests and exact-head CI pass.

required_actions.action: Bind the CODEX transcript's observed POST/response and replay tuple to the same authoritative requestClaim, with a cross-operation negative.
Publicly reconcile each exact child resource before COMMITTED/PASS and on terminal replay.
Implement and test bounded IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS recovery with frozen bytes and key.
